A step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is a function that can be written as a finite linear combination of indicator functions of intervals. That is, f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i \mathbb{I}_{[a_i, b_i]}(x), where a_i, b_i are real numbers and c_i are real numbers.

To prove that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable, we need to show that the upper and lower Riemann sums of f converge to the same limit as the partition of [a, b] gets finer.

Let P = {x_0, x_1,..., x_n} be a partition of [a, b]. Then, the upper Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by:

U(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n M_i (x_i - x_{i-1})

where M_i = \sup_{x \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]} f(x).

Similarly, the lower Riemann sum of f with respect to P is given by:

L(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n m_i (x_i - x_{i-1})

where m_i = \inf_{x \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]} f(x).

Since f is a step function, we can write f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i \mathbb{I}_{[a_i, b_i]}(x). Then, for each i, we have:

M_i = c_i and m_i = c_i

Therefore, we have:

U(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i (x_i - x_{i-1}) and L(P, f) = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i (x_i - x_{i-1})

Since the partition P gets finer, the summands (x_i - x_{i-1}) get smaller. Therefore, the upper and lower Riemann sums U(P, f) and L(P, f) converge to the same limit as P gets finer.

This shows that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable.
